exposure: Fetal hypoxic-ischemic insult (defined by umbilical blood pH < 7.1)
outcome: Glutamate-oxaloacetate transaminase (GOT) levels in umbilical arterial blood
Glutamate levels in umbilical arterial blood
cohort: A total of 46 newborn infants (28 females, 18 males) were included, comprising 23 control participants and 23 infants at risk of adverse neurological outcome (defined as umbilical blood with pH <7.1).
finding: Newborn infants with umbilical cord blood pH < 7.1 (indicating fetal distress) had significantly higher levels of both glutamate and glutamate-oxaloacetate transaminase (GOT) in their umbilical cord blood compared to newborn infants without fetal distress.
cross-section timing: At birth, from umbilical cord blood samples.
